title: Sara Finally Checked What Her $800 Gig Pays

scenes.say: Sara thought her weekend driving gig paid $20 an hour. It's closer to $11.
She drives about 40 hours a month and earns around $800.
So she finally did the math. That's about 1,000 miles, and gas and wear cost roughly $220.
Nobody withholds tax on gig money, so she sets aside about 25%.
Out of $800, she really keeps about $435.
That's $20 an hour, down to $14.50, then about $11.
Her fix: log every mile, skip long low-paying trips, and move 25% aside every week.
Do you know your real hourly pay? Subscribe, before $20 an hour quietly turns into $11.

description: Sara earns about $800 a month from a weekend driving gig and thought it paid $20 an hour. After roughly $220 of gas and car wear and about 25% set aside for taxes, she keeps about $435 — closer to $11 an hour. All numbers are rounded US estimates; tax set-asides vary by situation.
